subject: economics
title: Stagflation and Modern Inflation
welcome_lead: From the 1970s oil shocks to today's supply-driven inflation.
meta_desc: A-Level Phillips Curve: stagflation, supply shocks and modern policy.
final_note: Supply shocks push up inflation and unemployment together.

concepts.def: High inflation combined with stagnant output.
Sudden change in production cost (e.g. oil).
Beliefs about future inflation embedded in wages/contracts.
1980s aggressive US rate rises to break inflation.
Inflation expectations close to the target.

walkthroughs.body_html: The 1973 and 1979 oil shocks tripled fuel costs, raising inflation while crushing growth. Central banks faced an awful choice - tackle inflation and deepen recession.
US Fed Chair Paul Volcker drove rates above 19 percent in 1981, causing a sharp recession but crushing inflation expectations. The painful lesson: ignore inflation early, pay later.
2021 to 2023 saw a fresh round of supply-driven inflation - energy, chips, shipping. Central banks raised rates fast, hoping to anchor expectations before they drifted.
